title: DZELADINOV AND OTHERS v. "THE FORMER YUGOSLAV REPUBLIC OF MACEDONIA"
summary:
In Dzeladinov and Others v. "the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia," the applicants—Amdi Dzeladinov, Dudzihan Kamilov, Remzie Durmišova, Dagistan Alilov, and Mefail Asanovski—are Macedonian nationals of Roma origin, represented by the Association for the Protection of Roma Rights and the European Roma Rights Centre. The case focused on the vulnerability of Roma individuals to police violence and the lack of effective remedies for such abuses. On the night of 2 August 1998 in Štip, following a Romani circumcision celebration, the applicants and other Roma were allegedly subjected to violent police raids, including beatings, ethnic insults, and, in the case of the third applicant, mistreatment while seven months pregnant. Despite their complaints, the authorities failed to conduct an effective investigation into the alleged ill-treatment, and the applicants argued that their Roma identity was a factor in both the abuse and the lack of redress.

The European Court of Human Rights examined the case under Articles 3 (prohibition of inhuman or degrading treatment), 13 (right to an effective remedy), and 14 (prohibition of discrimination) of the European Convention on Human Rights. However, the Court ultimately found the application partly inadmissible, concluding that the applicants had not exhausted all available domestic remedies before turning to Strasbourg.

This case highlights the persistent barriers Roma and Traveller communities face in accessing justice and protection from police abuse. It reflects a broader historical context in which Roma and Travellers across Europe have struggled against systemic discrimination and institutional indifference to their rights.
